title: Banjar Council
summary: Modelled on the Balinese banjar, the neighbourhood council. The kulkul drum calls every household, and each sends one representative to the hall. The Kelian (head) guides musyawarah, talking until there is consensus. Then every household sends workers to the shared task: gotong royong, mutual help.
whenToUse: Decisions that affect every agent equally and work that needs everyone to contribute: shared conventions, a release day, a large refactor.
strengths: Consensus means everyone owns the result
Shared work after agreement builds goodwill
risks: Loud representatives can dominate a weak Kelian
Each meeting pauses the regular work

smileMetrics.cooperation: Households that sent workers to the shared task.
smileMetrics.harmony: Consensus reached with nobody standing aside.
smileMetrics.gathering: Time from the drum to the start of shared work.

communication: The drum reaches all households. Representatives speak in the hall in turn; the Kelian summarises each round until consensus. Then the Kelian assigns workers and the workers build the shared task.
cooperation: Cooperation = households contributing ÷ households, +1 for each offer taken into the consensus.
